by Bertha R. Hudelson

Strong Willow laid his sundried bricks with care,

As on the shadowed cliff he built his place;

And when the call of wild geese filled the air,

He spoke to Silver Star whose willow grace,

Veiled eyes, cheeks silken as a cactus bloom,

Had brought the dream his heart tried to express

Through beauty in the dim and simple room

Where life would warm its graywashed barrenness.

With winter food cached carefully nearby,

His hearth woodfilled and sturdy ladder done,

He led his willing bride four stories high

To love and laugh and wander near the sun....

He cannot know his silent room now brings

Awed reverence to seekers of past things.

Cliff Palace, Mesa Verde National Park, Colorado.
